title: A Short History of Africa in 3 Minutes

scenes.title: A Short History of Africa
facts: 54 countries
1.4 billion people
The longest human story on Earth
scenes.narration: Africa. Fifty-four countries, over one point four billion people, and the longest human story on Earth. Let's tell it in three minutes.

scenes.title: The cradle of humanity
facts: First Homo sapiens in Morocco and Ethiopia
Every human alive descends from them
scenes.narration: Our story begins here. Around three hundred thousand years ago, the first Homo sapiens walked the land that is now Morocco and Ethiopia. Every human alive today descends from these African ancestors.

scenes.title: Egypt, Kush and Aksum
facts: Pyramids, writing, a 3,000-year state
Kush ruled Egypt as its 25th dynasty
Aksum: trading power of the ancient world
scenes.narration: Five thousand years ago, along the Nile, Egypt rose: pyramids, writing, and a state that lasted three thousand years. To the south, the kingdom of Kush built its own pyramids and even ruled Egypt. In the highlands, Aksum became one of the great trading powers of the ancient world.

scenes.title: Iron, art and the Bantu expansion
facts: Nok terracotta sculptures, Nigeria
Ironworking spreads across the continent
Bantu languages reach the far south
scenes.narration: Meanwhile, across the continent, people were mastering iron. The Nok culture of present-day Nigeria sculpted striking terracotta figures, and Bantu-speaking farmers spread languages, crops and ironworking from West Africa all the way to the south.

scenes.title: Ghana, Mali and Songhai
facts: Caravans cross the Sahara
1324: Mansa Musa's pilgrimage moves the price of gold
Timbuktu: a city of scholars and books
scenes.narration: Then came the age of gold. Across the Sahara, caravans linked the empires of Ghana, Mali and Songhai to the Mediterranean. In thirteen twenty-four, Mansa Musa of Mali made a pilgrimage so lavish that it reshaped the price of gold in Cairo. Timbuktu became a city of scholars and books.

scenes.title: Swahili, Zimbabwe, Ethiopia, Benin
facts: Swahili cities trade with India and China
Great Zimbabwe: stone walls without mortar
Lalibela's rock churches, Benin's bronzes
scenes.narration: The whole continent was alive with states. Swahili city-states traded with India and China. Great Zimbabwe raised stone walls without mortar. Ethiopia carved churches from solid rock, and Benin cast bronzes that still astonish the world.

scenes.title: The Atlantic slave trade
facts: More than 12 million people taken
Societies shattered across the coast
A wound that still shapes the world
scenes.narration: Then a darkness. From the fifteen hundreds to the eighteen hundreds, the Atlantic slave trade tore more than twelve million people from Africa's shores. Societies were shattered, and the wound still shapes our world.

scenes.title: The Scramble for Africa
facts: 1884: the Berlin Conference divides a continent
By 1914 only Ethiopia and Liberia are free
Railways and borders, exploitation and resistance
scenes.narration: In eighteen eighty-four, European powers met in Berlin and carved up the continent on a map. By nineteen fourteen, only Ethiopia and Liberia remained independent. Colonial rule brought railways and borders, but also exploitation and resistance.

scenes.title: Africa fights back
facts: 1957: Ghana leads, under Kwame Nkrumah
1960: seventeen new nations in one year
1994: apartheid ends, Mandela is president
scenes.narration: Africa fought back. In nineteen fifty-seven, Ghana became the first sub-Saharan colony to win independence, led by Kwame Nkrumah. Nineteen sixty alone brought seventeen new nations. And in nineteen ninety-four, apartheid ended in South Africa with Nelson Mandela as president.

scenes.title: The story continues
facts: The youngest continent: median age 19
Music, film and technology go global
Three minutes is not enough
scenes.narration: Today, Africa is the youngest continent on Earth, with a median age of nineteen. Its music, film and technology travel the globe, and its story is still being written. Three minutes is not enough. But now you know where it begins.
